text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

An all-male panel chose a man over another man. The composition tells you nothing about your treatment — there's no sex-based difference between you and the person hired, so sex can't plausibly explain why he was preferred. Raising it would look like grasping, and would undercut the point you actually have.

Your real argument is substantive: on paper your PhD and nine years in risk modelling outrank a master's and vaguely described "regulatory affairs" experience. That's where to press.

So focus on the unanswered request. Send a short, firm follow-up to HR, referencing your original date, asking for the written reasons, the selection criteria, and how each shortlisted candidate scored. Silence after two weeks is the thing worth escalating.
